facts.raw_span: A 31-year-old male nursing student
history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previously treated his axillary condition successfully with 20% aluminum chloride
treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride was unsuccessful
used absorbent pads yet continued to soak through his pants
consequently unable to attend work
Minor starch-iodine test was performed
Areas of significant sweating were identified in the sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)
a 10 × 3-cm grid was drawn on the sacrum and a 6 × 8-cm grid was drawn on the intergluteal cleft
with the outermost dots omitted

concepts.why: The patient has a history of axillary hyperhidrosis and is now experiencing excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum.
The patient's excessive sweating is not attributed to any underlying medical condition, suggesting primary hyperhidrosis.
The patient's excessive sweating is localized to specific areas, including the intergluteal cleft and sacrum.
The patient's excessive sweating in the intergluteal cleft and sacrum did not respond to treatment with 20% aluminum chloride.
It explains the excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, which is an unusual location for primary hyperhidrosis.

rationales.F02: History of axillary hyperhidrosis suggests a predisposition to hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F03: Excessive sweating of the buttocks is a strong indicator of hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F04: Successful treatment of axillary hyperhidrosis with aluminum chloride suggests that the patient's condition is not entirely treatment-resistant.
rationales.F05: Unsuccessful treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride suggests treatment-resistant hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F09: The Minor starch-iodine test results confirm the presence of significant sweating in the sacral and intergluteal regions, indicating hyperhidrosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's excessive sweating is localized to specific areas, including the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, which supports the diagnosis of Focal Hyperhidrosis.
